active_location.macro_silhouette: The Magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz shear ripped across the volatile ferrofluid sea, throwing erratic arcs of raw energy into the bruised twilight. Jagged basalt pinnacles jutted like teeth against the roiling, magnetic tide, glowing faintly under the barrage. The barometric pressure fluctuated wildly, turning the horizon into a smeared, deafening painting of kinetic fury that tasted of ozone and oxidized copper.

sensory_palette.sight_and_color: Violet lightning and shifting obsidian ferrofluid
sensory_palette.sound: Deafening, rhythmic roaring of magnetic shear

interactive_features.affordance_description: A tall natural pillar vibrating with the shear
A glowing cluster of nitrogen-fixing moss
Swirling currents in the magnetic sea

reactive_toys.motivation_goal: Equilibrate the planetary magnetic field by force
reactive_toys.consistent_method: Striking unprotected metallic structures and biological entities

narrative_prose: Kaio clung to the vibrating side of the Resonant Basalt Spire, his breath hitching as the Magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz shear roared overhead. Violet lightning crawled down his arms, making the brass sextant in his grip feel almost alive against the copper tang of static on his tongue. He had to ATTRACT the Bioluminescent Mycelial Node's glow, coaxing it into a readable path, but the ferrofluid sea below was churning too wildly. The shear was deafening, smelling of ozone and oxidized copper, and the uncomfortably warm air pushed him to CONCEAL himself behind a jagged outcropping. He sketched frantically, trying to DEFEND his fragile parchment from the wind. He scrambled up the spire, whistling a three-note bird call to steady his nerves, and reached the safety of the upper ridge. He shoved a handful of glowing, nitrogen-fixing moss into Ryn's calloused hand. 'Look at the eddy patterns! You can use this for the braised mire-lentils!'
